text: 🇲🇽✊ "It's not about people being at the service of the economy, but about the economy being at the service of people." "Humanism, in essence, is a government of the people. (...) Our model, rather than copying models from other parts of the world, comes from our own history." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 26, 2026 Asked how she would sum up Mexican humanism, Sheinbaum cited more than 17 million Mexicans lifted out of poverty, recognized by the World Bank. New data out today: the share of the population in labor poverty fell from 34% to 30%, and real per capita labor income grew 9.3% in a year. She called the well-being programs "love for the people turned into public policy": direct transfers based on new rights, like the pensions for older adults, women and people with disabilities. The minimum wage is up 154% as the transformation turns 8 years old on December 1.

text: 🇲🇽⚖️ "Between 25,000 and 35,000 children and adolescents live in care centers. 7 out of 10 are ready to be adopted, but they can't be because of the cumbersome procedures." "If we have a right but no way to make it effective, we don't really have the right." — Arturo Zaldívar, Coordinator of Politics and Government of the Presidency, Mañanera, Nov 26, 2026 Sheinbaum signed and sent to the Senate today a reform of the National Code of Civil and Family Procedures. Family cases are 4 in 10 cases in state courts. It creates a special abandonment trial with a hearing in 25 days, full adoption nationwide, and a safe, penalty-free way to give a baby up for adoption. Divorce is decreed in a single hearing, with child support from the start based on real income: judges can check the SAT and banks. On vicarious violence: protection within 24 hours, visits suspended and no mediation with the aggressor. It would take effect the day after publication, not in 2031.

🇲🇽📊 <u>Labor Poverty Hits a Record Low: 30.5%</u>

INEGI: the share of Mexicans whose labor income can't buy the basic food basket fell to 30.5% in Q3 2026, the lowest since the series began in 2005. That is 3.8 points down in a year; El Economista calls it the biggest annual drop since 2021. Rural labor poverty fell to 43.1% and urban to 26.9%, both record lows. Real per-capita labor income rose 9.3% to 3,656 pesos.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum on the DEA's Snitch Lines in Sinaloa and Jalisco: "It's Interference"</u>

The DEA has opened hotlines for Mexicans to report alleged cartel members, partners and officials in Sinaloa and Jalisco. Sheinbaum's reply: "Imagine if the SSPC opened a WhatsApp line to report corruption in the United States. How would the US government see it? It is clearly a matter of interference." Washington, she said, should focus on the corruption and drug-trafficking networks operating inside its own country.

🇲🇽🏗️ <u>GDP Grew 3.3% in Q3, the Fastest Since 2023, Driven by Public Works and Housing</u>

INEGI's final figure: the economy grew 0.9% quarter on quarter and 3.3% year on year from July to September, its strongest pace since 2023. Construction output jumped 15.7% a year, fueled by Infonavit, Fovissste and Conavi housing and by public works. Services grew 3.6% and industry 2.7%. Sheinbaum noted these are numbers "that no international financial institution, not even a national one, wanted to recognize."

🇲🇽🔬 <u>4,335 Mexican PhDs Applied for 200 Research Jobs</u>

Secihti's 2026 job-placement call had 4,335 applicants for 200 positions, so only 4.6% could get in. Contralínea's José Romero argues that the language of "merit" turns a structural shortage into personal failure: "A better thesis or another paper won't turn two hundred positions into four thousand." There were 676 applications for local histories of peoples and communities alone. The state funds doctoral training, but the jobs still have to follow.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico and Brazil: Pemex and Petrobras Move Closer, No Free-Trade Treaty Needed</u>

Latin America's two biggest economies are building a trade partnership that protects producers on both sides rather than signing a classic free-trade deal. Pemex and Petrobras already have a memorandum of understanding on exploration, production and industrial processes. Mexico wants Brazil's deepwater know-how in the Gulf through a mixed-investment model that stays within its Constitution. Sheinbaum and Lula agreed by phone to reciprocal visits, and she may attend his January 5 inauguration.

🇲🇽🚀 <u>Sheinbaum Puts SpaceX's Texas Launch Site on the Table</u>

Every Starship launch from Starbase needs Mexico to authorize a slice of its airspace and clear it of other flights. Sheinbaum has already raised it with the US embassy and is now seeking a meeting between both countries' aviation authorities. With talk of up to 400 launches a year, Mexico wants to decide how often it grants that permission, "and if necessary, the relocation of the launch zone." Profepa is still reviewing the Starship debris collected on Playa Bagdad on November 17.

🇲🇽⛽ <u>Customs Revenue Up 12% in October, Even While Subsidizing Every Liter of Fuel</u>

Mexico's customs agency, ANAM, collected 124,409 million pesos in October, 12% more than in September, on a pricier dollar and 6% more operations. VAT at the border hit 92,871 million and import duties hit 20,232 million, both the highest of the year.

The one tax that fell was IEPS, down 23%, because the government is using it to hold down pump prices. The fuel stimulus has cost 61,337 million pesos in customs revenue since March, according to ANAM. (El Economista)

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Regulator Fines Salinas Pliego's TV Azteca for Keeping Investors in the Dark</u>

Mexico's banking and securities commission, the CNBV, fined TV Azteca 2,688,600 pesos for withholding information from investors in 2021. That was the pandemic year when the network struggled to pay its dollar debt and issued 12 "relevant event" notices about swings in its share price and trading volume.

The fine was imposed on October 8 and only came to light through La Jornada. TV Azteca says it will challenge it. The $400 million in notes it set out to "reorganize" in 2021 is now being litigated in a New York federal court, and the company delisted from the Mexican stock exchange in March. The obligations from its years on the exchange still apply.
